EMERGENCY NOTE   Date: 2026-09-13
35F, emergency department visit after a missed medication dose.

S:
Patient presents to the emergency department after realizing this morning that she left her anticonvulsant at home while visiting family and missed last night's dose. She has had no episodes and feels at her usual baseline. She would like today's dose and enough tablets to get home in two days. She reports good adherence otherwise and uses a medication alarm on her phone. No shortness of breath. Sleep has been shorter than usual during the trip, about 6 hours a night. Sister with schizophrenia. She works as a teacher and returns to work on Monday. Lives with her spouse, who came with her today. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 118/74, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 99% on room air.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Neuro: alert and oriented, speech fluent, normal strength and sensation, steady gait.
Labs (today): basic metabolic panel within normal limits, anticonvulsant level at the low end of the therapeutic range.

A/P:
1. Epilepsy, seizure-free on current medication for 8 months. Missed dose given in the department. Prescribed a 3-day supply at her usual dose to cover the trip home. Reviewed keeping a spare supply in her bag and protecting her sleep while traveling. Her neurologist was messaged with today's level and will review it at the next visit.
2. Safety: reviewed when to return for care and to avoid driving until she has resumed her usual schedule.
3. Family history: noted for the record; no change to today's management.

Discharged home in stable condition with her spouse. Follow up with her neurologist as scheduled, sooner if any new symptoms occur.
